title: Quantized surge gate and commitment declivity reconciler
author: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: spikes in tenant demand produce noisy, continuous adjustments to reserved capacity which increase evictions and oscillation. This PR introduces two coordinated features aimed at stabilizing short-term surge behavior and gracefully decaying commitments when utilization falls: 1) a Quantized Surge Gate (QSG) that only allocates burst capacity in discrete quanta to reduce churn in the allocation surface, and 2) a Commitment Declivity Reconciler (CDR) that introduces a smooth, utilization-driven decay curve for tenant reservations to avoid cliff-style decommits. Scope: runtime admission controller, fleet autoscaler hooks, metrics/telemetry, unit and integration tests, and docs/feature-flag wiring. Implementation notes: - Quantized Surge Gate: new config fields in fleetconfig: surge_quantum_tokens (default 128 tokens), min_quanta_retention (default 1), and surge_lease_ttl_ms. QSG batches burst grants into fixed quanta and prefers to assign from an ephemeral surge bank before touching steady reservations. This reduces per-request churn in the reservation ledger and produces more stable utilization signals. - Commitment Declivity Reconciler: introduces a declivity_index per-tenant (float) computed from smoothed utilization percentile and recent request slope. When utilization drops below threshold, we apply a conservative exponential decay with a tunable floor and backoff. The reconciler also emits a suggested_release signal rather than an immediate release for multi-pass verification. - Telemetry: new Prometheus metrics: redwood_qsg_quanta_issued_total, redwood_qsg_quanta_consumption_rate, redwood_cdr_declivity_index, redwood_cdr_suggested_release_total. Added tracing spans for qsg.assign_quanta and cdr.evaluate_tenant. - Safety: feature gated behind feature_flags.quantized_surge_v1; default off for existing customers. Includes conservative defaults and a canary rollout path in the autoscaler config. - Tests: unit tests for quanta math and backoff, an integration test that simulates a 2-minute burst followed by a 15-minute cooldown to validate no sudden decommit spikes, and a soak test workload to assert invariants on eviction counts. - Docs: design doc (docs/runtime/quantized-surge.md), runbook snippets for on-call, and a short example for Dedicated teams to opt in. Checklist: [x] design doc checked in [x] unit tests added [x] integration tests added [x] observability wired [x] feature flag gating added [x] changelog entry drafted Related: ENG-2047 (stability post-burst), ENG-2211 (eviction metrics reduction).

review_comments: Diego Ruiz: Nice clean split between QSG and CDR; one ask - can we rename surge_quantum_tokens -> surge_quantum_size? the term 'tokens' collides with other tokenized accounting. Also please add a unit test for fractional quanta rounding.

Samir Banerjee: Tests look good, but I'm concerned about the default quantum size for small tenants. Suggest adding per-tenant max_quantum fraction so a single tenant can't consume disproportionate burst bank. Also noticed two linter warnings in autoscaler/declivity_reconciler.go.

Evelyn Cho: Telemetry shape looks reasonable. Can you ensure that suggested_release is a counter and emits a label for reason (util_below_threshold|manual_override|quota_pressure)? Also add an alert query in docs for sudden increase in quanta_consumption_rate.

Asha Menon (author): Thanks all - I renamed the config to surge_quantum_size, added tests for fractional rounding, and added per-tenant max_quantum_fraction with sane defaults. Fixed lint issues and switched suggested_release to a labeled counter. Updated docs with the alert example. Pushed changes in commits d0e1f2b..f6g7h8i.
Diego Ruiz: Approving after the naming/labels change. Marking as approved for merge when CI green.
Samir Banerjee: Approved (verified integration test pass locally).
release_notes: Introduce Quantized Surge Gate (QSG) to stabilize burst allocations by issuing discrete quanta and Commitment Declivity Reconciler (CDR) to smoothly decay tenant reservations when utilization drops. Feature is off by default and gated behind quantized_surge_v1. Observability: new metrics for quanta and declivity indices. Impact: reduced eviction churn during spikes; opt-in for Dedicated fleets.
